title: Republican Palace Museum
geometryBasis: The 12-point OpenStreetMap outline fixes the approximately 57 m by 25 m cruciform shell. Schultz’s 1915 plan places the separate campanile to the southwest and shows the covered passage linking it to the church.
sectionBasis: The 1912 account specifies yellow and pale-red sandstone, green glazed roof tile, deep eaves, two feet from ground to terrace and four feet from terrace to the church floor. The west drawing shows the pointed portal, clustered rose lights, hoods, and the separate clock and belfry stages.
limitations: The museum exterior represents the 2007 phase on an approximate prewar reconstruction. Finish and form follow the original drawings and published material descriptions.

The exact finished tower dimensions, roof height, lantern treatment, east and north openings, and the extent of the historical terrace are estimates. The tower’s original published plan supplies its location within the grounds.
floorBasis: The terrace and church floor follow the two-foot and four-foot rises stated in 1912, tied to the unchanged source terrain at the west approach. Foundation walls meet the original field along the nave and transepts.
